A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-task training experiments, mechanistic measurements, and pretrained Gemma and Llama analyses, including supplementary experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds learning-rate controls, E-KAR evaluation, task variants, and representation-probing experiments.

M1.justification: The core Transformer architecture and final-token cross-entropy objective are unchanged. Appendix Q adds a trained and evaluated variant that replaces explicit entity/functor queries with partial entity tuples. Appendix P extends the input formulation to multiple distinct functor tokens. These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic relational tasks and artificial LLM prompts. v4 adds natural-language analogy evaluation on E-KAR with Gemma-2-9B, plus scenarios with noisy structural correspondences, multiple categories and mappings, and implicit-functor queries (Appendices N-Q). These substantially broaden the represented domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: v1 uses logit-lens decoding without a learned-readout comparison. v4 Appendix R and Figure 25 directly compare it against a trained per-layer linear probe. This adds a diagnostic comparison method; the original Gemma and Llama model coverage is retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include a four-layer learning-rate sweep over 10^-5, 10^-4, and 10^-3; a fixed 100-entity comparison across two, four, and five categories; E-KAR source/candidate-pair measurements; and trained linear and bilinear probes. These substantially expand the evaluation design. The previously reported default architecture and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds targeted checks of optimization-related depth failure, imperfect structural correspondence, dependence on a single mapping and explicit functor cues, logit-lens readout limitations, embedding-norm effects, and bilinear relational structure (Appendices B and O-T). These extend the original sensitivity and geometric analyses and test several previously unresolved assumptions.

E5.justification: Both versions state in Section 2.2 that reported results are averaged over three random seeds. v4 provides no revised run-count statement or newly specified uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure. Shaded result curves already appear in v1.

E6.justification: The original result plots and prompt-probability entries are retained, while v4 adds substantial new findings: deeper-model recovery with learning-rate tuning, E-KAR layer-wise trends, noisy and implicit-mapping performance, and probe results. Appendix T reports 81.1% bilinear-probe accuracy and a null-space ratio falling from 0.624 to 0.108. These are newly reported results, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The original task definitions and Dirichlet-energy derivation are retained, with Appendix F becoming Appendix G. Appendix T adds a bilinear relation score and a normalized null-space-ratio definition, ||Wf|| divided by the mean of ||We_i||. This is a limited mathematical addition; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about delayed analogy emergence and the two-component mechanism remain. Section 3.3 narrows the depth-scaling claim to fixed optimization settings, acknowledging recovery through tuning. The new conclusion explicitly extends the claimed empirical validation to a natural-language analogy benchmark.

C2.justification: v4 replaces the main text's inverse-depth-scaling interpretation with an optimization-dependent account. It also explains earlier linear decodability, warns that embedding norms influence Dirichlet energy, and expands the limitations discussion to acknowledge primarily correlational mechanistic evidence and partially tested real-world assumptions (Section 7; Appendices B and R-T).

D1.justification: v4 adds an implementation-code link in Section 3 and construction details for the new noise, multiple-functor, and implicit-query experiments. Appendix A's hardware, architecture, and default training tables are retained. Documentation improves modestly, although the new probes lack detailed training and evaluation split specifications.

R1.justification: The main analogy and structure-mapping positioning remains. v4 adds references concerning grokking progress, synthetic-task interpretation, and causal interventions, including Nanda, Furuta, Noroozizadeh, Wang, and Wurgaft. It removes the McKenzie inverse-scaling reference and the introductory Qwen and Grok references. These are localized positioning changes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and appendix discussions are retained with local editing and revised explanations. The limitations material from v1 Appendix L is reorganized and expanded into Section 7, followed by a new Conclusion and Impact Statement. The narrative changes are localized despite the substantial added experimental content.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating figures. v1 Figure 3 becomes v4 Figures 3-4, and v1 Figure 7 becomes Figures 8-9. Captions are expanded, and new appendix Figures 11 and 21-27 display the added analyses. Retained plots largely preserve their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens the evidence and its interpretation. The depth-specific learning-rate control corrects an overbroad inverse-scaling interpretation, while E-KAR and relaxed-assumption experiments address important validity gaps. Readout and embedding-norm checks identify confounds, and the expanded limitations make the lack of causal validation explicit. New probe protocols remain sparsely documented, but the gains in experimental support and interpretive caution are substantial.
